headline: Administrators and school secretaries push for contracts after 505 days without one
summary: Speakers for the Waltham School Administrators Association said the cost of living offer is 2.5%, which they called too low. Speakers for the school secretaries said their contract expired July 1, 2025, and asked for a full budget audit. A parent described a student safety concern at Waltham High School. The committee voted to ask the mayor for $254,000 for the 617 Lexington Street transformer project.
decisions: Approved asking the mayor for $254,000 to finish the 617 Lexington Street transformer project.
Approved keeping school closed on Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Good Friday, citing staffing concerns.
Tabled the Waltham Public Schools disciplinary data report.
Approved an interim assistant superintendent for finance and operations for this school year.
Approved posting the assistant superintendent for finance and operations job as soon as possible, with the mayor abstaining.
Approved paying the bills on the warrant.
discussion: Administrators' contract talks: Speakers said the group has worked 505 days without a contract and that prices in greater Boston rose more than 3% in each of the last two years, above the 2.5% offer. They asked the committee to bargain in good faith and settle the contract.

School secretaries' contract and budget: Speakers for the 35 school secretaries said their contract expired July 1, 2025. They said the school budget ran over by $864,596.08 and asked for a public itemized explanation and a supplemental appropriation for retroactive pay.

Student safety at Waltham High School: A parent described messages sent to a 14-year-old freshman by an 18-year-old student and said the student was still attending the school. The parent said they would keep their child home and asked for enhanced security.

2027-28 school calendar: Members discussed a survey that drew 632 replies, mostly from caregivers, on holding school on Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur, and Good Friday. Members raised staffing coverage, impact bargaining with unions, and the 40.7% who said there should be no school on those days.

617 Lexington Street transformer funding: Project staff said an environmental spill extended the job and that about $254,000 more is needed. Members questioned whether another $39,000 for regulatory paperwork was needed, and a member asked for an itemized list of costs for the DL move.
